chapter: New Orleans halls and street bands
title: Halls and towns played with Carey and his own band
summary: National Park, Gulf Coast towns, local halls and white clubs, with Joe Gundolfi keeping him busy.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Where, where were some of the places you played when you were down here? When you first, some of the old halls, or what kind of jobs? Oh, well. When you had your own band, or Jack Carey, where'd you play?

Well, when I was, Jack Carey played in National Park the most of the time. National Park? Yeah, yeah, that's 3rd and Willow. 3rd and Willow. They've got a big school up there now, big school there. And we'd go out in like Gulfport, Biloxi, and all up there in Magnolia, Mississippi towns like that and play. And after I got my band, we the first band opened up their stores, my band. First band went up there. The hotel, okay. Yes, up over that hotel there. And we worked there a long time for beans.

And then I played Cooperators, Economy, and Napoleon Avenue Hall up there. I forget the name of that hall. And played the Frazarmi. I played the Santa Sinners. Oh, I played Freshman Hall. I played all around down there.
Was there anything going on out of Mellenburg in your days?

Oh, every Sunday in your birth. Every Sunday I'd go out in your birth. I used to play for a lot of white boys, you know, at clubs and things. I played for them all the time. There was a fellow named Joe Gundolfi, an Italian boy. He kept me working all the time. Kept me busy all the time.
